newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end firm, shrug off Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: German shares end firm, shrug off Wall Street.

text.p: German shares held their ground in the face of Wall Street's overnight weakness on Friday, reversing an early decline to end a thinly-traded bourse session higher.
Dealers said isolated buying interest in selected stocks had helped keep the market afloat, as had the firm dollar -- always a good signal for German exporters.
"Think of it this way -- the dollar is in our favour and interest rates here are still relatively low," said a Frankfurt dealer.
"We don't have as much to worry about as the U.S. right now. There is still a lot of liquidity in this market and very few long term investors who want to sell," he added.

The 30-share DAX index ended the day up 9.48 points at 3,359.29, nearly 40 points above its low of 3,321.32. The early decline came in the wake of the Dow Jones Industrials' 2.3 percent drop overnight on fears of higher interest rates.

The big movers of the day included engineering group Mannesmann, which came under selling pressure in early trade, but then rose from its lows after the company issued a statement saying its earnings would improve in 1997.

The early pressure came after a well-respected investment research house had downgraded the stock, dealers said. However Mannesmann ended the bourse session down 19 marks at 633, off a low of 617 marks.

Software group SAP bucked the downward trend from the start, with its preference shares rising 3.10 marks to 276.30 marks. SAP said on Thursday it saw no reason to depart from earlier forecasts of strong first-quarter profit growth.
Chemical shares were also firm, rebounding from lows hit earlier in the week after Hoechst shelved eagerly-awaited plans to list its HMR unit on the bourse.
And Daimler-Benz, one of the DAX's most dollar-sensitive shares, rose 2.70 marks to 129.15. Dealers said an analysts' meeting on Thursday had been taken up well in the market.
In addition, Daimler earlier announced plans for a joint venture with Deutsche Telekom to develop a traffic navigation system, which also attracted some interest.
